# Further reading {#further-reading}

Everything here is cited in one of the three source papers, or is a tool those
papers recommend. The list is grouped by task rather than by author.

::: {.tada-note}
Full bibliographic details for everything named on this page, and everywhere
else in the wiki, are in [References](#references).
:::

## The three source papers {#reading-start}

::: {.tabset}

### TADA {.unlisted .unnumbered}

**Ivimey-Cook, E. R., et al. (2025).** *TADA! Simple guidelines to improve
analytical code sharing for transparency and reproducibility.* EcoEvoRxiv.
<https://doi.org/10.32942/X2D93K> (preprint)

The four guidelines, the evidence for why they are needed, and worked "How To"
boxes for each letter with a pre-TADA and post-TADA code comparison. Includes a
one-page checklist as supplementary Figure S1.

Companion site: <https://eivimeycook.github.io/TADA/>

### SORTEE guidelines {.unlisted .unnumbered}

**Pick, J. L., et al. (2026).** *The SORTEE guidelines for data and code quality
control in ecology and evolutionary biology.* Peer Community Journal 6: e20.
<https://doi.org/10.24072/pcjournal.687>

Six stages of checks, written for journal data editors but the clearest
statement anywhere of what "good enough to archive" means. Also contains
suggestions for authors and for journals. Open access, CC BY 4.0.

### Code review {.unlisted .unnumbered}

**Ivimey-Cook, E. R., et al. (2023).** *Implementing code review in the
scientific workflow: Insights from ecology and evolutionary biology.* Journal of
Evolutionary Biology 36: 1347–1356. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jeb.14230>

The four Rs, how to write reviewable code, how code review fits at each stage of
publication, and a practical primer on starting a code club.

:::

## Guides to reproducible code {#reading-guides}

- **Cooper, N. & Hsing, P.-Y. (2025).** *Guide to Reproducible Code.* British
  Ecological Society. The standard field guide, and the one the SORTEE
  guidelines point authors to directly. (An earlier edition is cited as Cooper
  2017 by the TADA paper and as Cooper & Hsing 2017 by the code review paper.)
- **Abdill, R. J., Talarico, E. & Grieneisen, L. (2024).** *A how-to guide for
  code sharing in biology.* PLOS Biology 22: e3002815.
- **Filazzola, A. & Lortie, C. (2022).** *A call for clean code to effectively
  communicate science.* Methods in Ecology and Evolution 13: 2119–2128.
- **Sandve, G. K., Nekrutenko, A., Taylor, J. & Hovig, E. (2013).** *Ten Simple
  Rules for Reproducible Computational Research.* PLOS Computational Biology 9:
  e1003285.
- **Hunter-Zinck, H. et al. (2021).** *Ten simple rules on writing clean and
  reliable open-source scientific software.* PLOS Computational Biology 17:
  e1009481.
- **Sweigart, A. (2020).** *Beyond the Basic Stuff with Python: Best Practices
  for Writing Clean Code.* No Starch Press.
- **Jiménez, R. C. et al. (2017).** *Four simple recommendations to encourage
  best practices in research software.* F1000Research.
- **Patel, B., Soundarajan, S., Ménager, H. & Hu, Z. (2023).** *Making
  Biomedical Research Software FAIR: Actionable Step-by-step Guidelines with a
  User-support Tool.* Scientific Data 10: 557.

Also useful, and cited in the code review paper:
<https://coderefinery.github.io/reproducible-research/> and Lakens' chapter on
computational reproducibility,
<https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/14-computationalreproducibility.html>

## Code review literature {#reading-review}

- **Rokem, A. (2024).** *Ten simple rules for scientific code review.* PLOS
  Computational Biology 20: e1012375.
- **Hillemann, F., Burant, J. B., Culina, A. & Vriend, S. J. G. (2025).** *Code
  review in practice: A checklist for computational reproducibility and
  collaborative research in ecology and evolution.* EcoEvoRxiv.
- **Indriasari, T. D., Luxton-Reilly, A. & Denny, P. (2020).** *A review of peer
  code review in higher education.* ACM Transactions on Computing Education 20:
  1–25.
- **Fernández-Juricic, E. (2021).** *Why sharing data and code during peer
  review can enhance behavioral ecology research.* Behavioral Ecology and
  Sociobiology 75: 103.
- **Nakagawa, S. et al. (2023).** *Method reporting with initials for
  transparency (MeRIT) promotes more granularity and accountability for author
  contributions.* Nature Communications 14: 1788. Covers how to credit a code
  reviewer in the methods section.

## FAIR and open-science principles {#reading-fair}

- **Wilkinson, M. D. et al. (2016).** *The FAIR Guiding Principles for
  scientific data management and stewardship.* Scientific Data 3: 160018. The
  original, for data.
- **Barker, M. et al. (2022).** *Introducing the FAIR Principles for research
  software.* Scientific Data 9: 622.
- **Chue Hong, N. P. et al. (2022).** *FAIR Principles for Research Software
  (FAIR4RS Principles).* Zenodo. <https://doi.org/10.15497/RDA00068>
- **Lamprecht, A.-L. et al. (2020).** *Towards FAIR principles for research
  software.* Data Science 3: 37–59.
- GO FAIR's plain-language summary: <https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/>

## The evidence base {#reading-evidence}

Use these if you need to make the case to a co-author, a supervisor or an
editor.

- **Culina, A., van den Berg, I., Evans, S. & Sánchez-Tójar, A. (2020).** *Low
  availability of code in ecology: A call for urgent action.* PLOS Biology 18:
  e3000763.
- **Trisovic, A., Lau, M. K., Pasquier, T. & Crosas, M. (2022).** *A large-scale
  study on research code quality and execution.* Scientific Data 9: 60. The
  source of the 74% and 56% figures.
- **Kellner, K. F., Doser, J. W. & Belant, J. L. (2025).** *Functional R code is
  rare in species distribution and abundance papers.* Ecology 106: e4475. The
  source of the 93% figure.
- **Ivimey-Cook, E. R. et al. (2025).** *From policy to practice: Progress
  towards data- and code-sharing in ecology and evolution.* EcoEvoRxiv. The
  source of the 15%-to-88% journal-policy figures.
- **Kambouris, S., Wilkinson, D. P., Smith, E. T. & Fidler, F. (2024).**
  *Computationally reproducing results from meta-analyses in ecology and
  evolutionary biology using shared code and data.* PLOS ONE 19: e0300333.
- **Gomes, D. G. E. et al. (2022).** *Why don't we share data and code?
  Perceived barriers and benefits to public archiving practices.* Proceedings of
  the Royal Society B 289: 20221113.
- **Maitner, B. et al. (2024).** *Code sharing in ecology and evolution
  increases citation rates but remains uncommon.* Ecology and Evolution 14:
  e70030.
- **Vandewalle, P. (2012).** *Code Sharing Is Associated with Research Impact in
  Image Processing.* Computing in Science & Engineering 14: 42–47.
- **McKiernan, E. C. et al. (2016).** *How open science helps researchers
  succeed.* eLife 5: e16800.
- **Jenkins, G. B. et al. (2023).** *Reproducibility in ecology and evolution:
  Minimum standards for data and code.* Ecology and Evolution 13: e9961.
- **Archmiller, A. A. et al. (2020).** *Computational reproducibility in The
  Wildlife Society's flagship journals.* The Journal of Wildlife Management 84:
  1012–1017. The source of the conclusion-and-numbers criterion used in
  [code review](#review-four-rs).
- **Hardwicke, T. E. et al. (2021).** *Analytic reproducibility in articles
  receiving open data badges at the journal Psychological Science: An
  observational study.* Royal Society Open Science 8: 201494. The source of the
  percentage-error criterion.

## Tools {#reading-tools}

::: {.tabset}

### R {.unlisted .unnumbered}

| Tool | What for |
|---|---|
| **`here`** (Müller & Bryan 2020) | Relative file paths; see [Transferable](#transferable-paths) |
| **`renv`** (Ushey & Wickham 2023) | Project-level package environments; replaces `packrat`. Beyond the scope of TADA. |
| **`groundhog`** (Simonsohn & Gruson 2023) | Load packages as they were on a given date. Beyond the scope of TADA. |
| **`styler`** (Müller & Walthert 2020) | Reformat code to a standard style (tidyverse, Google) |
| **`testthat`** (Wickham 2011) | Unit testing |
| **`targets`** (Landau 2021) | Pipeline management; reproducibility hashes for expensive steps |
| **`workflowr`** (Blischak et al. 2019) | Reproducible project scaffolding and websites |
| **`codemeta`** (Boettiger 2017) | Generate standard code metadata |
| **`dataReporter`** (Petersen & Ekstrøm 2019) | Document and screen data quality |
| `sessionInfo()` | Base R; the environment section of your README |
| `citation()` | Base R; package citations with version numbers |

### Python {.unlisted .unnumbered}

| Tool | What for |
|---|---|
| **`pyprojroot`** (Chen 2023) | Relative file paths; the `here` equivalent |
| **`poetry`** (Eustace 2023) | Dependency management and packaging. Beyond the scope of TADA. |
| **`pipenv`** (Pipenv Maintainer Team 2023) | Reproducible environments. Beyond the scope of TADA. |
| **`pycodestyle`** (Rocholl 2022) | PEP 8 style checking |
| **`pytest`** (Okken 2022) | Unit testing |
| **`luigi`** (The Luigi Authors 2023) | Pipeline management |
| **`CodeMetaPy`** (van Gompel 2023) | Code metadata |
| **`cookiecutter`** (Feldroy 2022) | Project templates |
| **`setuptools`** | Package and version information |
| `session_info` | The environment section of your README |

### Environments & pipelines {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Beyond the scope of TADA, but recommended where you have the appetite. This
covers all three categories the TADA paper names as beyond scope: dependency
and environment managers (`renv`, `groundhog`, `conda`, `poetry`, `pipenv` —
see the R and Python tabs), containerisation and workflow managers (below).

| Tool | What for |
|---|---|
| **Docker** (Merkel 2014; Boettiger 2015) | Containerisation; a complete, portable software environment |
| **Singularity** (Kurtzer et al. 2017) | Containerisation, common on HPC systems |
| **Snakemake** (Köster & Rahmann 2012) | Workflow management; defines step order and dependencies |
| **Nextflow** (Di Tommaso et al. 2017) | Workflow management |

A curated list of pipeline tools: <https://github.com/pditommaso/awesome-pipeline>

### Choosing a licence {.unlisted .unnumbered}

| Resource | For |
|---|---|
| <https://choosealicense.com/> | Code licences: MIT, GPL, BSD, Apache |
| <https://choosealicense.com/no-permission/> | What happens with **no** licence |
| <https://chooser-beta.creativecommons.org/> | Data licences: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-NC |

:::
